sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: No market-priced extremity going into the week — every macro-signals series sits below the ±2 z-score "extreme" threshold. The two strongest elevated readings are the S&P 500 (z=+1.86) and Nasdaq 100 (z=+1.84), both stretched versus their 3-year averages after a strong run. Gold (z=+1.56) and 20y+ Treasuries (z=-1.56, i.e. elevated long yields) round out the elevated set, but neither crosses into extreme territory. Over the past month the S&P 500 climbed from 7,413 to 7,677 (+3.6%), consistent with the elevated z-score rather than any acute stress.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.62% median (151 tickers, 2,626 news items — a thick window), though none of this week's covered reporters sit in that sector. Copper follows at +2.63% median across just 6 tickers (247 news items), and oil-gas sits at -1.92% median on 33 names with a thick 1,161-item news window. Among this week's actual reporters, industrials (+1.28% median; AVAV/CPRT/SAIC) is the strongest matching cohort.
